title: Distinguish absent scheduling state from corrupt continuation evidence
summary: Durable continuation readers must initialize only on proven absence and preserve malformed or inaccessible evidence before scheduling and recording turns.
reusable_steps: Durable continuation readers must initialize only on proven absence and preserve malformed or inaccessible evidence before scheduling and recording turns
expected_outcome: When a durable cursor determines fair scheduling, use a local strict reader: classify only an initial governed ENOENT metadata result as absence, then validate a regular file through the shared JSON reader and pure shape predicate. Reject parsing, access, metadata and subsequent read failures, including falsy JSON and disappearance after existence was observed. Preserve the original evidence and require operator inspection; an optional reader that returns null on all errors silently resets scheduling. Reuse the same semantics in read-only diagnostics, sanitize errors, and revalidate under the existing recording lock because ordering and recording may be separated. This is not filesystem compare-and-swap against noncooperating writers. Validate actual isolated effects, attempts, byte preservation and fresh-process fairness; normalize fault-injection paths with path.join for Windows portability. Keep authenticated recovery and scoped execution policy separate from cursor blockage.
